Paper_Metadata.Paper_Title: Zwitterionic Engineering of Vinylene-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks for Superior Protonic Electrolytes

Composition_Info.Material_Name_Raw: Zwitterionic vinylene-linked COF (ZVCOF) functionalized with sulfobetaine moieties
Composition_Info.Note: Synthesized by Knoevenagel condensation between 1,3,5-tri(4-formylphenyl)triazine (TFPT) and N-sulfopropyl-2,4,6-trimethylpyridinium (SPTMP). Features sulfobetaine zwitterionic functionalities.

Process_Text.original: ZVCOF was synthesized through a Knoevenagel condensation reaction between 1,3,5-tri(4-formylphenyl)triazine (TFPT) and N-sulfopropyl-2,4,6-trimethylpyridinium (SPTMP).
Process_Text.simplified: Knoevenagel condensation of TFPT and SPTMP to form vinylene-linked COF with sulfobetaine functionalities.

Microstructure_Text.original: PXRD patterns revealed high crystallinity. Pawley refinement indicates eclipsed AA stacking model. Characteristic diffraction peaks at approximately 5.6°, 9.8°, 11.4°, 15.0°, and 26.0°, corresponding to (100), (110), (200), (210), and (001) crystal planes. N2 adsorption-desorption isotherms showed typical type I behavior, suggesting microporous structures. BET surface area: 502 m²/g, pore volume: 0.29 cm³/g, pore diameter: 1.3 nm.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: Highly crystalline with eclipsed AA stacking. Characteristic PXRD peaks at 5.6°, 9.8°, 11.4°, 15.0°, 26.0°. Microporous with BET surface area 502 m²/g, pore volume 0.29 cm³/g, pore diameter 1.3 nm.

Properties_Info.Note: Poor conductivity due to insufficient proton sources

Composition_Info.Material_Name_Raw: Phosphoric acid-modified ZVCOF (PA@ZVCOF-80) with 80 wt% PA loading
Composition_Info.Note: PA incorporated into ZVCOF by mechanically grinding. 80 wt% PA loading. Maintains solid-state morphology. Highest proton conductivity among all COF-based electrolytes under ambient conditions.

Process_Text.original: Phosphoric acid (PA) was incorporated into the COFs by mechanically grinding the COFs with varying amounts of PA, resulting in a series of composites denoted as PA@ZVCOF-X (X = 40, 60, and 80, representing the mass percentage of PA).
Process_Text.simplified: Mechanical grinding of ZVCOF with phosphoric acid to achieve 80 wt% PA loading.

Microstructure_Text.original: PXRD analysis revealed diminished crystallinity with PA loading. Upon removal of PA via washing, diffraction patterns were restored, confirming structural robustness. N2 adsorption-desorption measurements showed very low BET surface area (9.6–26.3 m²/g) and pore volume (0.001–0.01 cm³/g), suggesting negligible residual porosity upon PA loading. FT-IR spectra displayed new absorption bands at 990 and 493 cm⁻¹ corresponding to P=O bonds, confirming PA presence.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: Diminished crystallinity with PA loading but structural robustness confirmed. Very low BET surface area (9.6-26.3 m²/g) and pore volume (0.001-0.01 cm³/g). P=O bonds confirmed by FT-IR.

Properties_Info.Note: Highest proton conductivity among all reported COF-based protonic electrolytes under ambient conditions
Low activation energy (< 0.4 eV) indicates Grotthuss-type hopping mechanism
Wide electrochemical stability window (2.7 V), significantly wider than 1.7 V for 5.0 M PA aqueous solution

Composition_Info.Material_Name_Raw: Phosphoric acid-modified NVCOF (PA@NVCOF-60) with 60 wt% PA loading
Composition_Info.Note: Non-zwitterionic counterpart synthesized from TFPT and 2,4,6-trimethylpyridine (TMP). 60 wt% PA loading. Shows inferior proton conductivity compared to zwitterionic ZVCOF.

Process_Text.original: NVCOF synthesized by Knoevenagel condensation between TFPT and TMP. PA incorporated by mechanical grinding.
Process_Text.simplified: Mechanical grinding of NVCOF with phosphoric acid to achieve 60 wt% PA loading.

Microstructure_Text.original: BET surface area: 937 m²/g, pore volume: 0.32 cm³/g, pore diameter: 1.7 nm for pristine NVCOF. With PA loading, similar low surface area and pore volume as ZVCOF composites.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: Pristine NVCOF has higher BET surface area (937 m²/g) than ZVCOF. With PA loading, similar porosity reduction observed.

Properties_Info.Note: PA@NVCOF-40 shows conductivities 10^-6 to 10^-4 S/cm. PA@NVCOF-60 shows 2-3 orders of magnitude improvement but still significantly lower than PA@ZVCOF.
Higher activation energy (0.22 eV for PA@NVCOF-60) compared to PA@ZVCOF (0.12-0.15 eV), suggesting less efficient proton-transfer process

Composition_Info.Material_Name_Raw: Solid-state proton battery: MoO3 anode / PA@ZVCOF-80 electrolyte / H-VHCF cathode
Composition_Info.Note: Prototype solid-state proton battery assembled with PA@ZVCOF-80 electrolyte membrane (with 4 wt% PTFE binder), MoO3 anode, and vanadium hexacyanoferrate (H-VHCF) cathode.

Process_Text.original: PA@ZVCOF-80 was mixed with a small amount (4 wt%) of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder and processed into a membrane by rolling. The resulting membrane exhibits remarkable thermal stability, good mechanical flexibility, and can be easily bent or crimped without damage. SEM analysis discloses a dense and homogeneous morphology, with an overall thickness of approximately 100 μm. Prototype solid-state proton batteries were assembled by integrating the electrolyte membrane with a MoO3 anode and a Prussian blue analogue (vanadium hexacyanoferrate, H-VHCF) cathode.
Process_Text.simplified: PA@ZVCOF-80 mixed with 4 wt% PTFE binder, rolled into membrane (~100 μm thickness). Cell assembled with MoO3 anode and H-VHCF cathode.

Microstructure_Text.original: SEM analysis discloses a dense and homogeneous morphology. EDS mapping certifies homogeneous distribution of N, O, S, F, and P elements.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: Dense and homogeneous morphology. Homogeneous distribution of N, O, S, F, P elements confirmed by EDS.

Properties_Info.Note: Record-high specific capacity among all reported solid-state proton batteries
Reversible specific capacities: 108.5 (1.0 A/g), 98.6 (2.0 A/g), 92.6 (3.0 A/g), 88.3 (4.0 A/g), 84.3 (5.0 A/g) mAh/g
Excellent cycling durability with 90% capacity retention after 2000 cycles
High Coulombic efficiency maintained during cycling
Fast proton reaction kinetics indicated by high proton diffusion coefficient
